meta.description: Exposed to the agents as the `contain_host` tool. SIMULATES host isolation and posts a confirmation to Slack, so the approve→execute loop closes visibly without touching real systems. Swap the 'Simulate isolation' node for your EDR's API call when you go live.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ channel: $env.SLACK_DEFAULT_CHANNEL || '#incident-response', text: ':shield: [SIMULATED] Containment executed — ' + $json.action + ' on ' + $json.target, blocks: [ { type: 'section', text: { type: 'mrkdwn', text: ':shield: *[SIMULATED] Containment executed*\n*' + $json.action + '* → `' + $json.target + '`' } }, { type: 'context', elements: [ { type: 'mrkdwn', text: '`' + $json.incident_id + '` · ref `' + $json.containment_id + '` · network: ' + $json.network_access + ' · _no real system was modified_' } ] } ] }) }}

nodes.name: Confirm in Slack
nodes.notes: Set SLACK_BOT_TOKEN in the n8n environment. Falls through on failure so the tool still returns.
